name: Temple Emanu-El
note: Temple Emanu-El (1926, Arthur Brown Jr. with Sylvain Schnaittacher), own geometry from the Commons/Mapillary photos in docs/shots/refs/notable/emanu-el: cross-in-square sanctuary with four tiled gable arms (giant arched windows N/E/W, the great portal S on the courtyard), stepped buttress blocks, 16-bay drum and shallow terracotta dome to 45 m over OSM dome part way/1153003006; open courtyard with cloisters and an arched screen on Lake; 12 m front ranges, arched entrance pavilion, 15 m west wing. Placed by a Procrustes fit of the plan onto fit.ring (0.04 m). Photos over numbers: shallow dome (not a hemisphere), round 16-bay drum, open Lake Street screen. ~4.7k triangles.

name: The Ritz-Carlton
note: The Ritz-Carlton, 600 Stockton (1909 Metropolitan Life Building, Napoleon LeBrun & Sons), own geometry from the Commons/Mapillary photos in docs/shots/refs/notable/ritz-carlton: white terra-cotta block round the garden courtyard to a 30.5 m cornice, channelled walls, paired punched windows, rusticated barred ground storey; on Stockton (the plan west edge, found by a Procrustes fit onto fit.ring) a 5-column Ionic portico on a balustraded terrace over the drive with entablature and sculpted pediment, pilastered wings. Photos over numbers: five-column front spanning the whole 11.4 m jut, terrace ~7 m so columns run ~3 storeys.

name: Pier 43 Ferry Arch
note: Pier 43 Ferry Arch (1914 Belt Railroad ferry-slip headhouse), own geometry from the Commons photos in docs/shots/refs/notable/pier43-arch: a white boarded triumphal arch, 20.6 x 8 m block whose long edge (the plan's longest edge, found from fit.ring) is the face, one 9.6 m round arch through the thin dimension to 9.3 m with a 1.2 m archivolt to the ground, channelled outer piers, dentilled cornice at 11 m, shallow pediment gable to 14.8 m, 3 m plain annex at the end the plan bulges.

name: Malloch Building
note: Malloch Building (1936-37, Irvin Goldstine), 1360 Montgomery, Streamline Moderne "ocean-liner house", own geometry from the Commons photos in docs/shots/refs/notable/malloch: white four-storey block at Montgomery pavement (west edge found by a Procrustes fit of the OSM plan onto fit.ring, its 22 m street-parallel edge) with two garage floors showing downhill (fit.groundAt/grade), rounded corners, three wrap-around balcony bands with pipe rails, ribbon windows, entrance recess with ribbed silver band, silver sgraffito murals (worker, explorer, woman), roof terrace railings and a stair tower.

name: YWCA Residence Hall (940 Powell)
note: YWCA Residence Hall (1932, Julia Morgan), 940 Powell: red-brick eight-storey tower on a stone arched ground storey with YWCA belt course, stone-quoined piers up the front, a central stone top stage of arched windows under a tiled gable, tile-eaved wings; own geometry from the Mapillary photos in docs/shots/refs/notable/ywca.

name: St. Joseph's Hospital (355 Buena Vista East)
note: St. Joseph's Hospital (1928, Bakewell & Brown), 355 Buena Vista Avenue East, now condominiums: six-storey pink-beige stucco in stepped wings, red clay-tile hipped roofs per wing, round-arched base storey under a belt course, punched windows, cornice, a taller end pavilion; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/st-josephs.

name: Rialto Building (116 New Montgomery)
note: Rialto Building (1902, Meyer & O'Brien with Bliss), 116 New Montgomery at Mission: nine-storey buff-brick Renaissance Revival block with a light court, two-storey rusticated stone base with shop windows and an arched entrance, stone-framed window groups between brick piers, a frieze storey and a deep dentilled cornice; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/rialto.

name: Internet Archive (Fourth Church of Christ, Scientist)
note: Fourth Church of Christ, Scientist (1923), now the Internet Archive, 300 Funston: white Greek temple, six giant fluted Ionic columns across the Funston front before a recessed wall with three tall doors, deep entablature and attic with urns, wide steps; plain pilastered side walls with tall arched windows; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/fourth-church.

name: Paige Motor Car Co. Building (1699 Van Ness)
note: Paige Motor Car Co. Building (1919), 1699 Van Ness at Sacramento: cream terra-cotta auto showroom, giant round-arched ground arcade with dark infill and medallions, two storeys of big divided-light windows between piers, deep bracketed dentilled cornice; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/paige.

name: 650 Townsend (former Zynga HQ)
note: 650 Townsend (1990, former Zynga HQ): six-storey red-brick block with blue-glass bands between brick piers, rounded corners, a tall rounded drum at the Townsend/8th corner carrying a huge red panel with a white bulldog, open grey parking decks beside it; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/zynga.

name: The Pacific (2121 Webster)
note: The Pacific (2016 condominiums, former Pacific Medical Center): pale grey-beige panel block stepped 36 / 39.5 / 43 m over a stone podium, eight floors of windows in pale surrounds with a diagonal third of them projecting angled window boxes (two glass facets folded 0.55 m out, white wedge sill and hood), bronze corner piers, 8 m north wing and 10 m west strip; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/the-pacific. Part polygons cut from the outline to the OSM part areas.

name: Arched-crown office, King Street (way/149167950)
note: 2002 nine-storey red-brick office on King Street between 2nd and 3rd: dark storefront base, dark arched floors under a cream string course, big blue-grey windows, a set-back glass top floor under a shallow steel lens canopy and a curved brick crown wall with a round white emblem; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/w149167950.

name: 510 Townsend (Stripe)
note: 510 Townsend (Stripe HQ, 2019): six storeys of red brick with a deep grid of tall windows recessed behind proud piers, glazed ground floor with a dark entrance canopy, a dark-glass seventh storey set back ~3 m under an overhanging dark sloping roof; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/w496374691 (the 2010 LiDAR is of demolished buildings, ignored).

name: China Basin Landing – Berry Street Building
note: China Basin Landing, 185 Berry (converted 1920s Southern Pacific warehouse offices): ONE shared builder for both blocks, which are one design; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/china-basin: five storeys, the lower three a pale concrete frame of piers and floor bands round gridded blue-grey glass, a projecting band, then two bluer glass storeys stepped back 2.6 m; a railed plinth; on the long front a white arched entrance pavilion every ~60 m (8 m wide, 2.2 m over the roof, arched top window, square openings, steps). Photos over numbers: the stepped-back upper glass is from the photographs. Berry Street Building, front on Berry Street.

name: China Basin Landing – Wharfside Building
note: China Basin Landing, 185 Berry (converted 1920s Southern Pacific warehouse offices): ONE shared builder for both blocks, which are one design; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/china-basin: five storeys, the lower three a pale concrete frame of piers and floor bands round gridded blue-grey glass, a projecting band, then two bluer glass storeys stepped back 2.6 m; a railed plinth; on the long front a white arched entrance pavilion every ~60 m (8 m wide, 2.2 m over the roof, arched top window, square openings, steps). Photos over numbers: the stepped-back upper glass is from the photographs. Wharfside Building, front on the water.

name: Zinc-and-timber apartments, 8th & Brannan
note: Zinc-and-timber apartments, 8th & Brannan (2010s, six storeys round a courtyard): street fronts alternating bowed standing-seam zinc sections (custom curved panel strips, white-framed window ribbons, balconies) and flat brown timber-fin sections with deep punched windows, a big rounded zinc corner at 8th/Brannan, a glazed shop storey (Peet's, Trek) set back under everything, plain grey courtyard and slot walls; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/w15629071, plan and courtyard hole carried onto fit.ring by a Procrustes fit.

name: 200 Brannan apartments
note: 200 Brannan Street apartments (2000s, nine storeys): own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/w113103853 - long runs alternating pale grey panel (to 26 m, big white-framed multi-pane windows) and red-brown brick (to 23.3 m, tall paired windows, set-back grey top storey) on the OSM plan with its saw-tooth courtyard, dark glazed ground storey, and the green-grey glass corner tower (12 m square, 30 m) at Brannan/Delancey under a glass canopy on steel beams with upstanding fins. Placed by a Procrustes fit of the plan onto fit.ring. Photos over numbers: the crown is a pergola of parallel fins over a glass slab, not radiating blades.

name: 235 Second Street (former CBS Interactive)
note: 235 Second Street (CBS Interactive / CNET, 2001): brick blocks (four floors of square punched windows with stone sills over a stone plinth, a round-arched loggia at the two 2nd Street corners) interlocked with dark-green glass curtain-wall towers to 30 m under thin projecting flat canopy slabs, and a recessed dark-glass sixth storey under a canopy at 27 m; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/w80296730, front on 2nd Street (local -z).

name: 1650 Mission Street
note: 1650 Mission Street (former SF Planning Department, c.1990): five-storey civic block in light and dark grey banded stone with long ribbon windows, a big rounded corner at Otis/Gough wrapped by a blue-glass top storey under a thin roof edge, and a taller dark glass grid section at the far end of the Otis front; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/1650-mission.

name: Hotel Metropolis (Found Study), 2 Turk
note: Former Hotel Metropolis (Found Study), 2-16 Turk at Mason (1911, ten storeys): cream stucco block over a dark storefront base and two rusticated storeys, paired sash windows with light surrounds and shallow bays up the Turk front, a deep green-black flared cornice with a hipped cap, a black fire escape on the Mason face, a dark navy rear wall; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/metropolis, Turk front on local -z.

name: The Chateau (2701 Van Ness)
note: The Chateau, 2701 Van Ness at Greenwich (1929, seven storeys): cream stucco French Chateau apartment block, rusticated base with round-arched garage doors, paired windows, black fire escapes, and a steep dark slate mansard with pedimented dormers, cream gabled pavilions at the corners and tall chimneys to 30 m; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/chateau, Van Ness front on local -z, Greenwich on -x.

name: 2400 Pacific Avenue
note: 2400 Pacific Avenue at Fillmore (1932, eight storeys): cream stucco apartment block with canted bays stacked from the second floor, a dark slate mansard with pointed cream gables over every bay, a round-arched entrance under a stone balcony on the south-east corner tower, a red-brown fire escape and garage on Fillmore; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/2400-pacific, Pacific front on local -z, Fillmore on +x.

name: The Marker hotel (501 Geary)
note: The Marker (former Hotel Californian), 501 Geary at Taylor (1910s, nine storeys): buff-cream brick shaft, two-storey rusticated stone base of tall round-arched windows over a black plinth, a deep cream cornice and a higher corner pavilion with a pyramidal crown at Geary/Taylor; own geometry from docs/shots/refs/notable/w71504453, Geary front on local -z, Taylor on the adjacent edge.
